children: fell 4.4% in Thursday's trading after the Chilean miner reported a 7% increase in Q3 copper production and maintained its annual guidance but offered a tepid outlook for next year.
The company said it produced 151,900 tons of copper in Q3, up 7% Q/Q, driven by higher output at the Los Pelambres mine, which was temporarily shut down in July due to heavy rain and power outages.

cut its copper production expectations for FY 2026 to 625K-655K tons from previous guidance of 650K-700K tons, citing the stoppage at Los Pelambres; total YTD output was 436,900 tons, down 8.3% from the same period in 2025.

For FY 2027, the company said it expects copper output of 630K-690K tons in 2027 and lifted estimated cash costs before byproduct credits to $2.60-$2.70/lb from its previous expectation of $2.40-$2.60/lb, citing increased global diesel prices.

2027 production guidance implies no growth to the original guidance it gave for 2026, despite the expectation of a pickup in grades at Los Pelambres and the expected commissioning of a second concentrator at the Centinela mine, RBC Capital analysts Ben Davis and David Monus said in a note.
The guidance could drive mid-single-digit downgrades to consensus EBITDA for 2027, J.P. Morgan analysts said.

title: Antofagasta says Q3 copper output rose 7% but issues weak guidance
